s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pancreatic syndrome with recent onset of hyperglycemia and abdominal symptoms in a patient with a history of diabetes and cardiovascular disease
salient_findings: Elevated plasma glucose and hemoglobin A1c
Swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on imaging
key_facts: 67-year-old man with a 3-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus
Managed with metformin and glimepiride
Prior percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction 2 months earlier
40-year smoking history, quit after myocardial infarction
Four episodes of bloody diarrhea daily
No abdominal pain or fever
Normal white-cell count, bilirubin, and liver function tests
Plasma glucose rose from 258 mg/dL to 449 mg/dL
Hemoglobin A1c increased from 7.3% to 8.0%
Microalbuminuria of 50.7 mg/day
Anti–glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies were negative
Elevated serum amylase and lipase
Swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on contrast-enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography

shortlist.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on imaging

shortlist.label: Chronic pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of smoking and abdominal symptoms

shortlist.label: Pancreatic cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Recent onset of hyperglycemia and abdominal symptoms in a patient with a history of smoking

shortlist.label: IgG4-related pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and pancreatic swelling

shortlist.label: Drug-induced pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is taking metformin and glimepiride, which can cause pancreatitis

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of ulcerative colitis

shortlist.label: Acute interstitial pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent onset of abdominal symptoms and elevated pancreatic enzymes

shortlist.label: Chronic pancreatitis with acute exacerbation
shortlist.why_kept: History of smoking and abdominal symptoms with elevated pancreatic enzymes

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with swelling of the pancreas, elevated serum amylase and lipase, and the absence of abdominal pain or fever, along with the imaging findings of a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct, are consistent with IgG4-related pancreatitis. Additionally, the patient's recent onset of extensive ulcerative colitis and the lack of other clear causes of pancreatitis support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
rejected.why: While similar to IgG4-related pancreatitis, the lack of specific autoimmune markers and the presence of ulcerative colitis make IgG4-related pancreatitis a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic pancreatitis
rejected.why: The patient's acute presentation and lack of long-standing pancreatic symptoms make chronic pancreatitis less likely.

rejected.label: Pancreatic cancer
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of a mass or tumor on imaging, making pancreatic cancer less likely at this time.

rejected.label: Drug-induced pancreatitis
rejected.why: The patient's medications, including metformin and glimepiride, are not commonly associated with pancreatitis, and there is no clear temporal relationship between medication use and the onset of pancreatitis.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated pancreatitis
rejected.why: While the patient has ulcerative colitis, the pancreatitis appears to be a distinct process, and the diagnosis of IgG4-related pancreatitis better explains the pancreatic findings.

rejected.label: Acute interstitial pancreatitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging findings are not typical of acute interstitial pancreatitis, which is often associated with abdominal pain and more diffuse pancreatic inflammation.

rejected.label: Chronic pancreatitis with acute exacerbation
rejected.why: The patient's lack of long-standing pancreatic symptoms and the acute onset of pancreatitis make this diagnosis less likely.
